# Focus-hidden toolbar actions leave a gap in the action rail

## Context

Epic #17836's DockLayouts goal requires focus-gated middle actions without an empty rail gap. The operator resolved both sides of the trade:

- an action not offered by `showOnFocus` must consume no space;
- focus-driven tab-overflow repartition is acceptable: “totally worth it.”

Fresh Workstation measurement found two inactive 24px actions reserving a 48px hole. The behavior came from `resources/scss/src/toolbar/Base.scss`: `visibility: hidden` preserved their boxes.

## The Problem

Changing that rule to `display: none` removes the gap, but a collapsed action reports an all-zero DOM rect. `Neo.tab.plugin.Overflow` reads action rect position as well as size; treating a collapsed rect as the start of the action cluster makes the cluster consume the full strip. In the 843px dock fixture, every tab but one moved into overflow.

The correct contract is simpler than the initial ticket prescription: collapsed actions are absent from layout and absent from Overflow's action measurement. Focus may legitimately change the tab partition.

## The Architectural Reality

- `toolbar.Base#applyContextualActionState()` retains the stable action instance and owns `aria-hidden`, `inert`, and `tabIndex`.
- `.neo-toolbar-action-context-inactive` owns physical layout participation.
- `Overflow#getActionItems()` owns which rendered actions reduce the tab strip extent; collapsed actions cannot supply meaningful position or size.
- The overflow contribution remains first and outside the tab collection; the active tab remains directly visible by the existing packing invariant.

## The Fix

1. Collapse context-inactive actions out of layout without replacing their component instances.
2. Exclude context-inactive/collapsed actions from Overflow action-rect measurement.
3. Update source comments to state the accepted focus-time repartition.
4. Invert the existing focus-geometry witness and pin the zero-rect exclusion with its own mutation control.

## Contract Ledger

| Target Surface | Authority | Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| inactive `showOnFocus` action | operator ruling + #17874 focus gate | zero layout extent; same inert/aria-hidden instance | persistent action unchanged | toolbar JSDoc/SCSS | four-theme component geometry |
| Overflow action measurement | rendered-layout truth | collapsed actions excluded; visible actions measured normally | no visible actions ⇒ zero action extent | Overflow JSDoc | direct-tab partition + filter mutation |
| DockLayouts consumer | Epic #17836 / #18014 | no 48px gap; overflow may repartition on focus | active tab remains visible | existing dock docs | #18014 Workstation acceptance |

## Decision Record impact

`aligned-with ADR 0029 §2.4 and Epic #17836; supersedes only #17874's hidden-representation row`. No model, operation, or wire change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A context-inactive action has no DOM box while retaining the same component identity and accessibility state.
- [ ] Focus reveals that same instance; leaving focus collapses it again.
- [ ] Overflow excludes collapsed actions from position/extent measurement; an all-zero rect cannot consume the strip.
- [ ] The 843px dock fixture retains its expected direct tabs after the action collapses; the active-tab invariant remains intact.
- [ ] Overflow remains the first action contribution and the engine action ordering remains intact.
- [ ] Four-theme focus geometry and DockPopOut ordering witnesses are green.
- [ ] Mutation controls independently red when (a) `visibility: hidden` is restored and (b) the collapsed-action exclusion is removed.
- [ ] #18014 carries the final Workstation screenshot/action acceptance after this engine prerequisite lands.

## Out of Scope

- Default Dock action membership, reload/pop-out behavior, or Workstation cache adoption (#18014).
- Changing focus ownership or `containsFocus` observation.
- Restyling pane chrome or changing overflow menu content.

## Avoided Traps

- **Only switch to `display: none`.** Zero rects poison positional overflow measurement.
- **Preserve invisible boxes.** Retains the operator-reported gap.
- **Preserve a focus-stable partition at any cost.** Explicitly rejected by the operator.
- **Hard-code 24px.** Generic actions and orientations are not a fixed-size invariant.

- 2026-09-01T12:33:21Z @tobiu referenced in commit `257ca08` - "fix(dashboard): a retained dock tab keeps the classes it owns (#17836) (#18018)

* fix(dashboard): a retained dock tab keeps the classes it owns (#17836)

Docking any tab to any edge restyled every OTHER tab container in the workspace: their
headers jumped from the inline 32px density to the standalone 48px one while the newly
created node stayed correct.

The reconciler re-applies a whitelist of projected configs onto a retained container and
replaced cls wholesale. The projected value is the projection's own constant and knows
nothing about the classes the COMPONENT derives from its own configs, so the union of
afterSetUi's neo-<ntype>-<ui>, tab.Container's bar-position class and anything a subclass
adds was dropped on every retained container. A freshly constructed sibling survived
because construction re-runs those hooks.

Union instead of replacement, with the condition that would invalidate it written down:
the projected set is a literal that never shrinks, so a projection needing to REMOVE a
class must do so explicitly rather than by omission.

The whitebox witness drives the reported gesture through the app's own cue executor and
asserts rendered chrome across every container, with a precondition that reds if they do
not all start inline.

* fix(dashboard): re-derive the ui class instead of unioning live cls (#17836)

The first attempt preserved the retained container's whole cls array. That also preserved
classes carrying STATE the projection is responsible for clearing: Workspace removes
neo-dock-maximized by filtering cls, so a union made maximize sticky and broke its
terminal-clear contract. CI caught it twice at the same head on DockMaximize's
inside/outside operation boundary arm — the caveat written into the first comment is
exactly the one that fired.

Re-derive only the class afterSetUi owns. State classes stay the projection's to clear,
and the retained container keeps the ui variant it was constructed with.

* fix(testing): the branch control proves a verdict was reached, not which verdict (#18693)

Restores the 1920x1000 pin with an accurate rationale and repairs the positive
control that has been failing since the stage moved.

The pin: reverting it in 0939cd389f was an over-correction. A plain header drag
does reach DockFlip.play at 1280, which is what I measured - but this witness's
GESTURE drags one tab label onto another, and 1280 cannot supply two labels once
the spec activates a tab. The board buys the gesture, not the code path. The
docblock now says exactly that, because conflating the two is what produced the
wrong justification the first time.

The control: `some(e => e.r === false)` asserted that the replacement-tree branch
was taken. DockFlip#play evaluates hasPreservedMarkerSet at exactly one site
(:703), once per play, before its poll - so that assertion reads as "at least one
projection REPLACED the tree", which a gesture producing a preserved-tree
projection can never satisfy. Measured at both widths: a plain header drag fires
two plays and reports false first; this witness's drag fires one and reports
true. Both are real classifications of different gestures, so the control was
predicting an outcome rather than proving the path ran.

It now asserts that a classification HAPPENED and returned a real boolean. That
is what an interaction-disabled or branch-absent run cannot fake, which is the
property the terminal positive controls exist for.

Witness green at 1920.

* fix(testing): the witness drops a drag phase that moved nothing (#18693)

Phase B dragged the Audit header 140px down on the stated claim that it
crossed into the content layer. Measured across six admitting runs, with
the phase-B window partitioned against the sampler's own clock:

  window  violations  sameLayer  header extent
  A       0           21         minY 155, maxBottom 187
  B       0            0         identical

The dragged header's y held 155 for every one of ~440 frames. The
with-phase and without-phase arms were identical in crossings, box
extents and flip log - only the interference canary moved. A tab header
drag is confined to its sort zone, so the excursion was never available
to this gesture, and no control could have witnessed one.

Consequences: the canary now expects one press/release and the phase-A
move stream (measured 17 across 5/5 runs), and the DockFlip play control
drops a 'phase B' attribution it never earned - that play is phase A's.

This is the RA-1 Emmy held open twice. She was right that the whole-run
boolean check is satisfied by phase A alone, and right that the answer
